samples.text: In this age of digital innovation, we must address the emerging divide between the global South and the global North. With the evolution of artificial intelligence, that divide risks becoming wider still. The United Nations should work towards

eliminating barriers to the digital economy in Africa, such as the high costs of Internet services and intellectual property rights. Furthermore, there is a need to work towards common global standards to regulate cryptocurrency trading platforms. That is the most effective way to provide confidence in those new markets and limit the potential for instability. Our own experience in Nigeria, as in other countries, shows that new technologies, when not properly regulated, can facilitate organized crime, violent extremism and human trafficking. In our own case, the trading of cryptocurrency helped to fuel speculation and undermined macroeconomic reforms.

This effort combines renewable energy, clean cooking, and gas as a transitional fuel with climate-smart agriculture and nature-based solutions, finance, must be governed by equity and shared responsibility, rather than charity, with international commitments translated into accessible, predictable, and adequately funded mechanisms that enable developing countries to pursue climate action without compromising development objectives. Excellencies, we refuse to surrender our technological future to paranoia. An invention can be destructive or beneficial, depending on the purpose it serves. and the judgment of those who use it. A knife can take life in the hands of an assailant and can save one in the hands of a surgeon. We can deploy artificial intelligence to wage war or use it to transform healthcare, education, agriculture, governance, and economic productivity. Much of the anxiety surrounding AI reflects the distrust we have allowed to grow amongst us. Nigeria is investing in digital public infrastructure, broadband connectivity, innovation systems, research institutions, and technology intellectual ownership. We invite the world to augment resourceful and enterprising young people to direct AI towards humanity's advancement rather than its destruction. Mr. President, one of the greatest obstacles to sustainable development is inadequate financing. Many developing countries devote substantial resources to debt servicing at the expense of education, healthcare, and infrastructure. Nigeria, therefore, calls for reform of the international financial architecture, wider access to concessional financing, and debt sustainability frameworks that recognize developmental needs. We also support innovative financing through private capital, blended finance, South-South cooperation, and strategic partnerships for sustainable development climate adaptation, and resilient infrastructure. Nigeria further recognizes the African Continental Free Trade Area as one of the continent's most transformative opportunities. It can strengthen regional value chains, expand intra-African trade, promote industrialization, and attract investment. Africa must move beyond its historical role as an exporter of raw materials toward greater value addition. manufacturing, technological innovation, and knowledge-driven growth. Our abundant natural resources must become engines of shared prosperity rather than sources of perpetual dependency. Mr. President, no nation, however formidable its defenses, can secure itself completely against dangers sustained beyond its borders.
